analysis.closest: Direct psychology breadth across social, cognitive, biological, clinical, lifespan and health courses plus experiments, statistics, evidence synthesis and qualitative methods. Sociology and philosophy support explanatory breadth. The psychological core outweighs narrower gaps in professional practice, test construction and specialised clinical neuropsychology.
analysis.clinical: Four distinct courses give complementary population health, drug action, pathology and ethical inquiry on a shared strong psychology base. Assessment and psychotherapy remain genuine subject coverage.
analysis.brain: Seven to nine distinct choices relative to the other options include computational, lab and life-science contributions; retain the cognitive neuroscience spine, data handling, machine learning and experimental language study. The computing elements bring complementary methods rather than implying an exact psychology match.

constructionStop: Three supported and feasible options. A social/work alternative is evidenced by direct interests and curriculum choices but is outside the authorised three-option maximum.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Academic writing, literature evaluation, research questions and reflective communication; common academic foundation.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: Operationalisation, measurement, sampling, design and introductory statistical inference; practical group research project.

DISDATA111.name: Introduction to Data Science
DISDATA111.contribution: R data cleaning, wrangling and visualisation prepare the brain option for computational analysis.

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning
DISDATA211.contribution: Regression, classification, validation and model evaluation support predictive inquiry; not the full psychology inference sequence.

DISDATA212.name: Image Processing & Computer Vision
DISDATA212.contribution: Filtering, segmentation and recognition give the brain option an engineering perspective on visual information; not human vision training.

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.contribution: Normative argument and ethical analysis broaden the clinical option, independent of psychology research ethics.

GOSPHIL214.name: Philosophy of Mind
GOSPHIL214.contribution: Mind, consciousness and identity provide conceptual foundations in the broad option.

GOSPHIL311.name: Philosophy of Emotion
GOSPHIL311.contribution: Philosophical theories and appraisal of emotion complement empirical affective psychology.

GOSPHIL313.name: Free Will, Time & the Self
GOSPHIL313.contribution: Agency, responsibility and determinism deepen analysis of explanation and choice in the broad option.

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.contribution: Institutions, identity and stratification place behaviour in social context.

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: Qualitative design, interviews, interpretation, ethics and reflexivity support social and health questions.

GOSSOCI311.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
GOSSOCI311.contribution: Trust, participation and social capital extend social analysis from individuals and groups to institutions.

HCBBIOM111.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
HCBBIOM111.contribution: Study designs, patterns, association, bias and confounding inform population-health questions.

HCBBIOM211.name: Functional Anatomy
HCBBIOM211.contribution: System and spatial anatomy support physiological explanations; not clinical skills training.

HCBBIOM311.name: Pharmacology
HCBBIOM311.contribution: Drug action, kinetics and toxicity give a biomedical perspective on intervention in the health option.

HCBBIOM313.name: Mechanisms of Disease
HCBBIOM313.contribution: Organ dysfunction and disease mechanisms provide health context, not a dedicated psychiatric module.

HCBCOGN112.name: Neurobiology
HCBCOGN112.contribution: Comparative neuroanatomy, regulatory behaviour and animal-research ethics ground biological explanations.

HCBCOGN212.name: Perception & Action
HCBCOGN212.contribution: Sensory processing and goal-directed action contribute human cognitive neuroscience; clinical case assessment is a gap.

HCBCOGN311.name: Higher Order Functions
HCBCOGN311.contribution: Attention, memory and executive control with cognitive experiments connect brain function and behaviour.

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.contribution: Description supports language acquisition, comprehension, production, aphasia and hands-on experimental approaches. Positioned after the brain and behaviour gateway.

HCBGATE101.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
HCBGATE101.contribution: Cells, metabolism, communication and heredity underpin physiology and biomedical study.

HCBGATE102.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
HCBGATE102.contribution: Neural signalling, learning, personality, social behaviour and mental disorders give foundational breadth.

HCBLIFE211.name: Molecular Cell Biology
HCBLIFE211.contribution: Gene expression, signalling and cell physiology provide mechanisms for later lab and disease study.

HCBLIFE212.name: Human Physiology
HCBLIFE212.contribution: Homeostasis, nervous and endocrine systems connect brain and behaviour with whole-body function.

HCBLIFE214.name: Life Science Laboratory
HCBLIFE214.contribution: Biochemical, microbiological and molecular practicals give the brain option experimental tools at a different scale from behavioural research.

HCBLIFE311.name: Molecular Pathology & Genetics
HCBLIFE311.contribution: Cell injury, pathology, heredity and genetic diagnosis help connect molecular variation to disease; no inferred behavioural-genetics practicum.

HCBPSYC111.name: Social Psychology
HCBPSYC111.contribution: Social cognition, attitudes, groups, prejudice and interpersonal influence give direct social psychology coverage.

HCBPSYC211.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
HCBPSYC211.contribution: Experimental design, regression and group comparisons directly contribute behavioural statistics.

HCBPSYC212.name: Psychopathology
HCBPSYC212.contribution: Biopsychosocial psychopathology, classification and case-based reasoning contribute clinical breadth.

HCBPSYC311.name: Medical & Health Psychology
HCBPSYC311.contribution: Health behaviours, stress, illness and care decisions support applied health psychology.

HCBPSYC312.name: Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies
HCBPSYC312.contribution: Reliability, validity, assessment interviews and psychotherapy contribute direct clinical overlap; Groningen trains a specific professional interview sequence.

HCBPSYC313.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
HCBPSYC313.contribution: Systematic review, study selection, effect sizes and meta-analysis contribute advanced quantitative synthesis, separate from original empirical data collection.

HCBPSYC314.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
HCBPSYC314.contribution: Physical, cognitive, emotional and social development from prenatal life to later life anchors the lifespan strand.

HCBPSYC315.name: Youth Resilience to Extremism
HCBPSYC315.contribution: Interdisciplinary study of youth radicalisation, protective factors and educational prevention applies social and developmental concepts.

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.contribution: Framing, argumentation and persuasive messages extend social influence into applied communication.

alignment.rationale: Both develop academic reading, writing, presenting and reflective study skills; UCR also emphasizes personal and civic formation.
Both introduce psychological theories and scientific approaches to behaviour; Groningen provides a dedicated Psychology survey and methods course.
Both examine social cognition, groups, attitudes and interpersonal influence, with Groningen adding explicit cross-cultural psychology.
Groningen covers scientific objectivity, replication and causation. UCR Philosophy of Mind studies mind and consciousness.
Both cover research design and research ethics. UCR concentrates on qualitative inquiry, while Groningen extends psychological experimental design.
Groningen practises professional conversation, listening and group skills. UCR Persuasive Communication focuses on how messages influence people.
UCR addresses self, emotion and behaviour across courses but lacks a selected dedicated personality-and-individual-differences course.
UCR integrates historical context within courses but lacks a selected dedicated history-of-psychology module.
UCR includes social behaviour and organisational context but lacks a selected dedicated workplace-psychology course.
UCR provides professional development but lacks a selected dedicated professional-orientation course within Psychology.
Both introduce descriptive statistics and how to interpret data. UCR also covers sampling, measurement and research design.
Groningen runs a first-year practical with psychology experiments and research participation. UCR research courses offer other ways to practise methods.
Groningen offers a dedicated introduction to statistical inference. UCR covers parts of inference across its research and statistics courses.
Both develop inference, regression and comparisons of means using behavioural research data.
UCR includes statistical modelling and predictive methods. Groningen teaches a separate third psychology statistics course.
Both integrate a research question, design, data analysis and reporting. UCR synthesises existing studies, while Groningen students design a supervised empirical project and collect data.
UCR covers psychological assessment and statistics but lacks a selected dedicated psychometric test-theory course.
Groningen requires a 15 EC psychology research thesis. The optional UCR research opportunity is displayed separately from the scheduled credits.
Both apply psychological theory and evidence to practical problems; UCR centres health, stress and illness.
Both examine psychopathology, classification and explanations of mental disorders.
Both examine psychological development across the lifespan.
Both address assessment and diagnosis; Groningen includes communication practice while UCR also examines psychotherapy.
Groningen requires 15 EC of restricted Psychology differentiation choices; UCR specialization is expressed through each complete selected curriculum rather than unassigned choice space.
Both examine neural and biological mechanisms underlying behaviour.
Both examine memory, attention, decision-making and higher cognition.
Both use evidence about the brain to explain behaviour. UCR focuses on perception and action, while Groningen introduces clinical neuropsychology and its disorders.
Groningen retains a genuine 30-EC university or personal minor; UCR flexibility is expressed through the complete selected 180-EC programmes rather than a separate unassigned block.

workbookScreen: Screened the active psychology and cognitive science course families against test theory, clinical training, statistics, professional practice and the three concepts. The direct assessment overlap in HCBPSYC312 is acknowledged; it is not counted again as a dedicated test theory course. BENGATE102 and HCBPSYC211 provide the clearest statistics overlap, with GOSSOCI212 strongest for research design and ethics. Advanced data electives support the brain concept without turning the separate Groningen Statistics III slot into an equivalence.
